name: rundrill-secure-coding
description: Secure-coding coach (OWASP) — find, exploit, and fix the vulnerabilities that ship in real code: injection, XSS, broken auth and access control, weak crypto, SSRF, deserialization, supply-chain and AI risks. Practised by reviewing AI-written code for security bugs, patching vulnerable code, and threat-modeling designs. Drills, progress, and mistake memory, inside your AI agent.

interface.shortDescription: Secure-coding coach: review AI code for vulns, fix vulnerable code, threat-model.
interface.longDescription: An interactive secure-coding coach (OWASP OCSD / ASVS) for working engineers. Walks the OWASP attack surface front to back across five areas — Foundations (threat modeling, secure design) → Input & Output (SQL injection, command injection, XSS, XXE, SSTI, file upload, path traversal, SSRF, mass assignment) → Identity (password storage, auth bypass, MFA, sessions, CSRF, access control, IDOR, JWT, OAuth) → Data & Crypto (AES, hashing, key management, TLS, HSTS, data protection) → Platform (REST/GraphQL APIs, CORS, security headers, business logic, supply chain, deserialization, secrets, CI/CD, logging, AI security). The risk it targets: AI writes insecure code by default, so the signature drill hands you plausible AI-written code with a planted vulnerability and asks you to find it, name the class, explain the exploit, and fix it — like a security pull-request review; plus fix-the-vuln patching, exploit-then-fix against your own local lab, STRIDE threat models, ASVS checklists, taint tracing, and SAST/SCA triage. Every fix is graded against the relevant ASVS control with mistake memory. Backed by the RunDrill MCP engine with progress tracking.
defaultPrompt: Show me some AI-written code and let me find the vulnerability.
